correctness.rationale: The two possible opposite-type cross-team exchanges have gain pairs (2x-a-d-1,2x-a-1) and (a-2x-1,a+d-2x-1). Their strict/weak conditions give the exact integer stability intervals, including d=0 equality. Welfare is 2[x(s-x)+(a-x)(t-a+x)] and has consecutive differences exactly twice the moving-pair gain sums; strict concavity makes TU-stability equivalent to global optimality. Each occupancy has binomial labeled multiplicity. Finite independent direct-payoff verification covers 155 parameter cells and 9,588 complete assignments with zero mismatches.

originality.rationale: The 2022 initiating paper defines the three exchange notions and gives general existence/price bounds, not an observed exact occupancy/counting theorem for two named tables with complete bipartite friendship. The new comparison concerns the conjunction of complete stable-set classification, precise TU=optimum equivalence, labeled counts, and sharp population thresholds 3 and 5. Full review of the originating technical body was limited by access; an equivalent unindexed result remains a stated priority risk.

value.rationale: Complete classification and labeled counts of three standard equilibrium notions on a natural heterogeneous-team network, plus exact welfare correspondence and sharp first strict-vs-ordinary (3 agents) and ordinary-vs-TU (5 agents) separations. Capacity disparity is a motivated structural parameter, not an arbitrary finite slice; formulas hold for every admissible positive population.
